claims.statement: Polish government guidance says a microinstallation connection must be reported to the relevant DSO no later than 30 days before planned start-up and points applicants to forms supplied by their own DSO.

The official Mój Prąd application guidance notes that different DSOs issue different connection-confirmation documents, providing a discovery-grade signal that document normalization is a real workflow problem.

contrary_evidence: DSOs already provide their own forms and portals, so submission itself is not a defensible product.
The cited Mój Prąd intake is closed; it supports document fragmentation, not current subsidy demand.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: founder-led proof inside one installer, followed by low-touch wholesale and training-channel referrals.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 350 branches at 1490 PLN monthly would produce about 6.3 million PLN ARR; durable retention and healthy margins could make founder-owned equity exceed 5 million PLN in years 5 to 7 without assuming a sale.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15 to 20 hours weekly for a narrow two-DSO pilot, with legal review outsourced.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 80% software gross margin after templates stabilize, with human review priced separately.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: fewer than three paid months if a channel partner yields at least four retained branches per 3000 PLN of enablement cost.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 249 PLN per dossier or 1490 PLN per branch-month after a free pilot.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: recurring because each new installation and every DSO form revision reopens the gate.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A consented rule graph linking DSO, hardware, form version, corrections, and eventual acceptance
fingerprint.customer: Polish photovoltaic and battery installers with repeated jobs across one or more DSOs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the family installer, then distribute through electrical wholesalers, inverter distributors, installer trainers, and trade accountants
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Vertical compliance SaaS with an optional paid human review and a signed dossier manifest
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays per dossier that passes internal preflight, or per branch-month for unlimited preflight
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A completed installation cannot be treated as grid-ready until the correct DSO dossier is complete and submitted

founder_fit: The founder can test the workflow inside the family renewable-installation company without broad networking.
Rules extraction, anomaly detection, and evidence lineage use data-science and AI leverage.
A software-first pilot is compatible with part-time work and controlled capital.
risks: A false pass could delay energisation and create contractual liability.
DSO harmonisation could erase much of the normalization wedge.
Installers may tolerate manual corrections rather than pay.

structure.control_point: Installer-issued signed preflight token before DSO submission and internal energisation release
structure.critical_dependency: Persistent DSO-specific requirements and lawful access to status or correction feedback

thesis: An installer-side preflight service could validate every grid-connection field and attachment, preserve who approved each datum, and issue an internal release token before a Polish solar or storage job is submitted to its distribution-system operator. The wedge is not another generic project manager: it is an auditable cross-OSD rules layer whose rejection and acceptance graph improves with every consented dossier.
title: OSD Commissioning Ledger for Polish Solar Installers
uncertainties: The frequency and cash cost of avoidable DSO rejections are unknown.
It is unknown which DSOs expose stable machine interfaces versus requiring user-mediated submission.
The 42000 PLN capital figure and all commercial figures below are bootstrap planning hypotheses, not observed results.
